case_title: Ravindra Tukaram Hiwale v. State of Maharashtra
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.498-A and s.306, sentenced to one year and four years respectively
high_court_outcome: Enhanced sentence under s.306 from four to six years
neutral_facts: The accused, who was married to the deceased, was alleged to have caused her death by burning. The prosecution claimed that the deceased suffered serious burn injuries in the kitchen around 7:00 a.m. on February 6, 1990, and later died from those injuries. The deceased made a dying declaration to a police officer on February 9, 1990, stating that she had quarreled with her husband over household chores and the feeding of children, then poured kerosene on herself and set herself on fire. The trial court convicted the accused under Sections 498-A and 306 of the IPC and sentenced him to one year and four years respectively. The High Court enhanced the sentence under Section 306 from four to six years. The Supreme Court quashed the High Court's enhanced sentence and confirmed the trial court's judgment.
